My friends who took his class before told me that he was very boring and speaking monotonously, making the class very boring and uninteresting; however I do not think that's the case. He was very nice to students and he was always willing to explain important concepts all over again every time we asked, even during breaks. He was not teaching monotonously-- I mean, calculus is very boring especially for an MBG student like me but he did his best to stimulate interest. He was also visibly disturbed whenever we used our phones in class, and even though he never snapped at us for that, his gaze at us was enough to feel disturbed so that we could stop playing with the phone. 

To summarize, I believe he is a very sweet teacher who helps students and who does his best to teach, pay no mind to bad evaluations. I've taken MATH 101 and 102 from Ozgun Unlu, Ali Sertoz, Mefaret Kocatepe and I can say that Serdar Ay was the most student-friendly teacher every and therefore I actually didn't suffer too much at his class. As an MBG student, I find this course too advanced for people of my department. While it is important to give us the necessary mathematical background to participate in effective research, there was not even one human being in entire MBG (including undergrads, master students, PHD students, professors and even people who work at industry) who told me that they have ever used Math 102 subjects in their research nor work life. Therefore, I find it unneccessary to put so much pressure on MBG students with a class that we are not going to actively use. The time (8-10 hours on average) I used to study for this class should have been invested in learning more about my major and important research, instead of this.

However, I do believe that there was one positive side of the course, which is to practice the written scientific communication. "Yes, this is true, but how can we prove it? Can we mathematically prove it for all the x?" type of mindset has deepened the insight I had about the theoretical part of science. If I was not extremely traumatized by math to the point I got nightmares, I'd thank Mr. Tekman, but no. Nevertheless, I think I'll pass this class this time, therefore, peace.
The course has a lot to teach and it can be basis for a lot of good math. However, it comes off as tiring sometimes
